item.title: Outshine Frozen Fruit Bars Recalled Over Glass Contamination Concern
item.description: The parent company, Dreyer’s Grand Ice Cream, voluntarily recalled five flavors nationwide. No injuries linked to the recalled products have been reported.
item.dc:creator: Alena Cerro
item.category: Dreyer's Grand Ice Cream Holdings Inc

item.title: Sugar Importer With Trump Ties Said to Maintain Abusive Labor Practices
item.description: A watchdog group said the Dominican company continued to violate labor standards after President Trump lifted an import ban last year.
item.dc:creator: Ana Swanson
item.media:description: Cutting sugar cane on a plantation in the Dominican Republic in 2023. Concerns over forced labor and human rights abuses in the Dominican sugar sector have existed for decades.

item.title: An A.I. Tax Boom Could Curtail America’s Debt. But Not Solve It.
item.description: The consequences of A.I. for the budget will largely hinge on whether — and to what extent — the technology reshapes the labor market.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Duehren

item.title: Gulf Oil Giants Push to Expand Overseas Stockpiles as Iran War Drags On
item.description: Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates are seeking larger oil reserves in Japan and South Korea as regional conflict threatens supply routes.
item.dc:creator: River Akira Davis
item.category: US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)
item.media:description: Storage tanks at an oil refinery, in Yokohama, Kanagawa, in Japan in April.

item.title: Home Depot Reports Higher Sales, but Its C.E.O. Isn’t There to Spread the News
item.description: Investors got a shock last week when the retailer said that Ted Decker, the chief executive, would take a medical leave. Tuesday’s earnings brought a more welcome surprise.
item.dc:creator: Jordyn Holman and Kim Bhasin
item.media:description: Ted Decker, the chief executive of Home Depot, in May. Last week, the company said he would take a medical leave of absence.

item.title: ABC Sues Trump Administration Over F.C.C. Threat to Its TV Licenses
item.description: The network asked a court to stop the agency from taking steps that could force ABC stations off the air and accused the F.C.C. of violating its First Amendment rights.
item.dc:creator: Jim Rutenberg and John Koblin
item.media:credit: Samuel Corum for The New York Times
item.media:description: The F.C.C. reviewed ABC’s television licenses after the network’s late-night host, Jimmy Kimmel, angered President Trump with a monologue joke.

item.title: Two Ships Transiting Strait of Hormuz Are Attacked as Oil Prices Rise
item.description: Maritime officials on Tuesday announced the recent attacks, which killed at least one sailor. Six months into the conflict, the vital waterway remains perilous.
item.dc:creator: Jenny Gross
item.category: US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)
item.media:description: Vessels near the Strait of Hormuz, as seen from Musandam, Oman, on Monday. Traffic through the strait has dwindled since the conflict began.

item.title: Is Silicon Valley in the Justice Dept.’s Sights?
item.description: Federal prosecutors are reportedly investigating Andreessen Horowitz, the venture capital giant, over board seats it holds.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Ross Sorkin, Bernhard Warner, Sarah Kessler, Michael J. de la Merced, Niko Gallogly, Brian O’Keefe and Sri Muppidi
item.media:description: Ben Horowitz, a general partner at Andreessen Horowitz.

item.title: Bond Sell-Off Sends Borrowing Costs to Highest Level Since 2007
item.description: Yields on the 30-year U.S. Treasury and government bonds across the world rose to multiyear highs as investors fret about inflation, deficits and A.I. spending.
item.dc:creator: Joe Rennison and Gregory Schmidt
item.category: US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)

item.title: At Ex-Premier Zhu Rongji’s Funeral, China’s Past Shadows Its Present
item.description: Beijing wants to portray today’s China as carrying forward Zhu Rongji’s era of growth, but for many Chinese, the optimism of that time has since faded.
item.dc:creator: Yan Zhuang
item.media:description: The Chinese flag flying at half-staff at Tiananmen Square in Beijing on Tuesday for the former premier Zhu Rongji.

item.title: What’s in an Airport Code? In West Palm Beach, It’s the President’s Initials.
item.description: The state’s Palm Beach International Airport has been renamed for the president, complete with a rare change in its three-letter airport code.
item.dc:creator: Christine Chung and Scott McIntyre
item.media:description: As of Aug. 18, the new name — President Donald J. Trump International Airport — has been fully adopted by the global aviation industry.

item.title: It’s Crunchtime Again for Canada to Avoid Trump’s New Tariffs
item.description: Canada is seeking a deal to dodge further economic pain at the hands of the Trump administration on midnight Tuesday. But at what cost?
item.dc:creator: Matina Stevis-Gridneff
item.media:description: The Gordie Howe International Bridge, connecting Windsor, Ontario, and Detroit, on the day after it opened last month. President Trump had threatened to block the bridge’s opening.

item.title: India’s College Boom Is Leaving Graduates in Debt and Without Jobs
item.description: Families are betting their savings on private universities as a path to a better life. A shortage of well-paying work is turning that wager into frustration.
item.dc:creator: Alex Travelli and Showkat Nanda
item.media:credit: Showkat Nanda for The New York Times
item.media:description: Students on the campus of Jamia Millia Islamia, a public university in Delhi, India. The country’s public universities are highly competitive, leading to the rise of private counterparts.

item.title: Paramount Asks States to Shoulder Costs of Delaying Warner Bros. Deal
item.description: Paramount’s $111 billion deal to acquire Warner Bros. Discovery has been postponed until the conclusion of a trial, a delay the studio says could cost it millions of dollars.
item.dc:creator: Lauren Hirsch and Benjamin Mullin
item.media:description: Paramount’s merger with Warner Bros. would create a Hollywood powerhouse.

item.title: ‘Buy Now, Pay Later’ Lenders Pitch Loans for Needs Like Electricity and Rent
item.description: The rapid growth of pay-later loans raises questions about whether their popularity is driven by consumer preference or desperation.
item.dc:creator: Stacy Cowley
item.media:credit: Loulou d'Aki for The New York Times
item.media:description: Americans spent $160 billion last year through pay-later loans from providers like Klarna — nearly twice the amount from just two years earlier.

item.title: Mark Cuban and Other Founders Wade Into Wealth Tax Debate
item.description: Some entrepreneurs, including Mark Cuban, are publicly worried about the potential fallout from California’s proposal to impose a special billionaire tax.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Ross Sorkin, Bernhard Warner, Sarah Kessler, Michael J. de la Merced, Niko Gallogly, Brian O’Keefe and Sri Muppidi
item.media:description: Mark Cuban, the investor and entrepreneur, has expressed his concerns that California’s wealth tax proposal could chill the state’s start-up culture.

item.title: A French Start-Up, Inbolt, Makes Robots See, and Work, Better
item.description: Inbolt, a French start-up that sells robot vision systems, helped a Stellantis plant in Detroit become a top performer in the company.
item.dc:creator: Farah Stockman and Sarah Rice
item.media:credit: Sarah Rice for The New York Times

item.title: As China Hunts for Scientific Talent, the US Makes It Easier
item.description: Young researchers have long come to the U.S. for academic training, but a combination of Chinese money and U.S. restrictions is shifting the balance.
item.dc:creator: Li Yuan

item.title: Should I Publicize a Bad Publicist?
item.description: Plus: An intern considers whether to give the boss an honest review.
item.dc:creator: Max Read
item.media:credit: Photo illustration by Margeaux Walter for The New York Times

item.title: How a False Nuclear Claim About Iran Ricocheted From India to Washington
item.description: A dubious post that spread on X became the basis of false claims that Iran’s leadership had declared it a nuclear power.
item.dc:creator: Steven Lee Myers, Ronen Bergman and Farnaz Fassihi
item.category: US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)
item.media:credit: Arash Khamooshi/Polaris for The New York Times
item.media:description: Funeral ceremonies for Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, Iran’s supreme leader, in Tehran in July.

item.title: As A.I. Data Centers Spread, Pressure Mounts to Share Profits
item.description: Policymakers around the country are maneuvering to ensure that tech giants aren’t the only ones who stand to benefit.
item.dc:creator: Tony Romm

item.title: 2 Planes With Same Call Sign in Phoenix Could Have Been ‘Disastrous’
item.description: An air traffic controller noticed that two planes — one departing, one landing — were both flight 2482. He acted quickly to avoid confusion.
item.dc:creator: Emmett Lindner
item.media:credit: Maansi Srivastava for The New York Times
item.media:description: “I’ve been working air traffic for 25 years — I’ve never seen two aircraft pretty much emerge with the same call sign,” the controller who discovered the overlap said.

item.title: The Cutthroat Wearables Battle Is About More Than Tracking Your Fitness
item.description: Google, Apple, Samsung and upstarts like Oura are racing to integrate data from their wearable devices into the health care system.
item.dc:creator: Brent Crane

item.title: Sports Team Sale Prices Keep Hitting New Highs
item.description: The deal for the Los Angeles Lakers valued the team at a record $12.5 billion, eclipsing the $10 billion paid for the franchise just last year.
item.dc:creator: Tania Ganguli
item.media:description: A statue of Kareem Abdul-Jabbar outside Crypto.com Arena, home of the Los Angeles Lakers.

item.title: Worker Pay Isn’t Keeping Up With Inflation Once Again
item.description: When prices spiked in 2021-22, wages failed to keep up for many workers, new research shows. Now the pattern is repeating.
item.dc:creator: Ben Casselman
item.media:description: The latest shock, driven by the jump in energy prices tied to the war with Iran, has sent measures of consumer sentiment tumbling.

item.title: How to Protect Your Home While You’re on Vacation
item.description: Store food in sealed containers and fix any leaking faucets or pipes, experts told our columnist, who had her own nightmare upon returning home.
item.dc:creator: Ann Carrns

item.title: How Cyclospora Evaded the U.S. Food Safety System to Sicken Thousands
item.description: The Trump administration delayed a rule last year that could have sped up the effort to pinpoint the source of the contamination. Critics charge that food safety oversight has eroded overall.
item.dc:creator: Christina Jewett and Julie Creswell
item.media:credit: Al Drago for The New York Times
item.media:description: Last year the Food and Drug Administration cut a program that tracked cyclospora outbreaks and delayed a rule that would have required companies to swiftly provide supply chain records in investigations of foodborne disease outbreaks.

item.title: FDA Classifies Egg Recall as Class I for Highest Health Risk
item.description: Nearly 20 million eggs were recalled in July over salmonella concerns. The new classification signals a “reasonable probability” of “serious adverse health consequences or death.”
item.dc:creator: Alena Cerro
item.media:description: Midwest Poultry Services voluntarily recalled 19 million eggs in July “as a precautionary measure,” the company said.

item.title: Hiroshi Okuda, Disrupter Who Revived Toyota in the 1990s, Dies at 93
item.description: As the car company’s president, he made decisions quickly and shook things up, expanding overseas manufacturing and introducing the Prius, a milestone in automotive history.
item.dc:creator: Clay Risen
item.media:description: Hiroshi Okuda sitting in the newly developed Prius in 1997. He pressed Toyota to finish the car, which had been in development for years, as other companies raced to be the first to introduce a hybrid.

item.title: Lawsuit Accuses Selena Gomez of Defrauding Investors in Mental Health Site
item.description: The actor, singer and beauty mogul founded Wondermind, a mental health platform, with her mother. Investors put in more than $1 million in the venture, which “quietly collapsed,” the suit said.
item.dc:creator: Remy Tumin
item.media:description: Selena Gomez and her mother, Mandy Teefey, at a panel focused on mental health during the SXSW conference in Austin, Texas, in 2024.

item.title: Google Turns On Gemini A.I. for Students Using Its Classroom App
item.description: Google enabled A.I. features for K-12 schools that have allowed student access to Gemini. Until this week, Google automatically enabled Gemini in Classroom only for students 18 or older.
item.dc:creator: Natasha Singer
item.media:credit: Ysa Pérez for The New York Times
item.media:description: Starting this week, a new Gemini tab within Classroom lets some students seek A.I. help on math problems and writing assignments; generate course aids like study guides, quizzes and flashcards; and produce images.

item.title: Outrage at UnitedHealth and Other Insurers Persists After Brian Thompson Killing
item.description: Higher premiums and rising medical bills have intensified Americans’ dissatisfaction with their medical coverage.
item.dc:creator: Reed Abelson
item.media:description: Stephen Hemsley, chief executive of UnitedHealth Group, left, was among the executives defending insurers’ practices at congressional hearings in January. To his left were David Joyner, chairman of CVS Health, and Gail Boudreaux, chief executive of Elevance Health.

item.title: Jeff Bezos Buys a Piece of Liverpool Football Club
item.description: It is the first known investment by Mr. Bezos, one of the world’s richest men, into a sports team.
item.dc:creator: Tania Ganguli and Theodore Schleifer
item.media:description: The deal values Liverpool Football Club at a little more than $7 billion.

item.title: July Retail Sales Notch Biggest Drop in Over a Year
item.description: The data for July showed the biggest drop in more than a year, as American households face the economic strains brought on by persistent inflation
item.dc:creator: Kim Bhasin
item.media:credit: Zack Wittman for The New York Times
item.media:description: U.S. shoppers spent less in July, as consumers struggled with persistent inflation, higher grocery bills and rising housing costs.

item.title: Amazon and Alphabet’s Profits Reveal Circular Nature of A.I. Boom
item.description: Investment gains at Alphabet and Amazon reveal a new way in which technology companies’ fortunes are increasingly linked.
item.dc:creator: Joe Rennison
item.media:description: Alphabet and Google have benefited from the rising value of their investments in A.I. companies, adding to profits beyond their core businesses.

item.title: Why Japan Is Struggling to Stop the Yen’s Decline
item.description: The currency has resumed its slide, eroding gains after the U.S. Treasury intervened to prop it up, as concerns mount about the direction of the country’s spending.
item.dc:creator: River Akira Davis
item.media:credit: The Yomiuri Shimbun, via Associated Press
item.media:description: The rally in the yen has faded, with the currency approaching 160 yen per dollar, a level that could test the resolve of officials in Tokyo and Washington.

item.title: The Markets Have Been on a Roll. Is It Time to Hedge Your Bets?
item.description: The S&P 500 is in position for a rare fourth year of consecutive double-digit gains. Risks are rising, our columnist says, yet Wall Street is doubling down.
item.dc:creator: Jeff Sommer

item.title: Robinhood Bets Again on a Public Venture Capital Fund
item.description: The trading platform raised $200 million for a second publicly traded vehicle to let ordinary investors buy into privately held start-ups.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Ross Sorkin, Bernhard Warner, Sarah Kessler, Michael J. de la Merced, Niko Gallogly, Brian O’Keefe and Sri Muppidi
item.media:description: Vlad Tenev, the C.E.O. of Robinhood, celebrating the I.P.O. of the Robinhood Ventures Fund I at the New York Stock Exchange in March. The company’s second venture fund began trading yesterday.

item.title: New Yorkers Can’t Stop Lining Up for This Sushi
item.description: At a proliferating number of stores, discounts on sushi and other items are offered after 8 p.m. To get the best meals, you have to be there early.
item.dc:creator: Emmett Lindner and Kareem Black

item.title: A Silicon Valley Dirt Farmer Hangs Up His Shears
item.description: Andy Mariani grows exotic and ethereally delicious stone fruit in the shadow of tech giants. But at age 80, it’s time to give up the land.
item.dc:creator: Carol Pogash and Ian C. Bates

item.title: How Pennsylvania Got Hooked on Games That Look a Lot Like Slot Machines
item.description: A legal loophole kept “skill games” from being considered gambling. Now lawmakers are trying to save them from a court ruling.
item.dc:creator: Leo Dominguez and Ben Blatt
item.media:credit: Hannah Beier for The New York Times

item.title: Kalshi Ordered to Cease Most Operations in Washington State
item.description: In a preliminary injunction, a state judge barred the prediction market from allowing residents to place bets on the bulk of its offerings.
item.dc:creator: Lauren McCarthy
item.media:credit: Eric Helgas for The New York Times
item.media:description: Washington is the latest state to successfully challenge prediction markets like Kalshi and Polymarket, which have grown rapidly.

item.title: Salvage Company Hoping to Sell Titanic Artifacts Challenges Court’s Role
item.description: A Virginia federal court has awarded the company the rights to collect, but not sell, items from the shipwreck. But the company says its earliest retrievals are governed by a French court.
item.dc:creator: Marc Davis
item.media:description: A company that has the rights to salvage items from the shipwreck of the Titanic is looking to sell 100 of the artifacts it has recovered at auction.

item.title: Flock Announces Privacy Updates to Its Car-Tracking Cameras
item.description: Critics say the measures are “public relations” and leave room for continued misuse.
item.dc:creator: Aruni Soni
item.media:description: A Flock Safety camera in Commerce City, Colo. The company’s technology is used by 7,000 U.S. law enforcement agencies.

item.title: Alfonso Fanjul Jr., Cuban American Sugar Baron, Dies at 89
item.description: With his brother, he presided over a family empire that includes the world’s largest cane sugar refiner and the Domino and C&H brands.
item.dc:creator: Trip Gabriel

item.title: In a Chinese Leader’s Death, Mourning for a More Hopeful Time
item.description: Tributes for former Premier Zhu Rongji reflect nostalgia for an era when China was opening to the world and the future seemed more prosperous and hopeful.
item.dc:creator: Li Yuan
item.media:description: Former Premier Zhu Rongji of China died on Wednesday. He was memorialized in Beijing.

item.title: How Bob Iger and Joshua Kushner’s Bromance Led Them to Lakers
item.description: Bob Iger, the former chief executive of Disney, and Josh Kushner, the venture capitalist, are buying the Los Angeles Lakers. Their wives set them up.
item.dc:creator: Brooks Barnes and Tania Ganguli
item.media:description: From left, the N.B.A.’s commissioner, Adam Silver, joined Joshua Kushner and Bob Iger at the 2025 U.S. Open tennis tournament.

item.title: Inside the $12.5 Billion Deal for the Lakers
item.description: The transaction, hashed out last weekend, reflects the huge profit potential of major sports franchises.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Ross Sorkin, Bernhard Warner, Sarah Kessler, Michael J. de la Merced, Niko Gallogly, Brian O’Keefe and Sri Muppidi
item.media:description: A proposed purchase of the Los Angeles Lakers by Josh Kushner and Bob Iger is a bet on the power of premier sports franchises.

item.title: What We Know About Taylor Farms’ Food Recalls
item.description: Just weeks after the company recalled lettuce and other produce suspected of being tainted by the cyclosporiasis parasite, it recalled jalapeños linked to a salmonella outbreak.
item.dc:creator: Kevin Draper
item.media:credit: Fred Ramos for The New York Times
item.media:description: Produce from Taylor Farms has been the subject of two recalls in recent weeks.

item.title: America Wants to Make Its Own Humanoid Robots. That Won’t Be Easy.
item.description: China already manufactures humanoid robots by the thousands. A new generation of U.S. start-ups is betting that there is still time to compete.
item.dc:creator: Meaghan Tobin and Amir Hamja
item.media:description: As a distributor for Unitree Robotics, Teddy Haggerty had a close-up view of China’s massive robotics industry. He also saw how much demand there was in the United States.
